digest:
Welcome to the latest PU Monthly Report, this time detailing all the development progress made throughout April. With the imminent release of Alpha 3.23, most teams began or continued tasks for events and releases coming soon and further into the year. Read on for the latest updates on jump points, weapon animation, the Anvil Legionnaire, and more.
- AI (Features): Throughout April, AI Features put significant effort into the Alpha 3.23 release, specifically the kopion creature that will be found across planetary surfaces and in caves.
- AI (Tech): Last month, AI Tech focused on planetary navigation mesh, with the version implemented recently receiving significant improvements.
- Animation: In April, the Animation team worked on various creatures, including two predators and a prey animal.
- Art (Characters): In April, the Character Art team began work on two specialist armors, reworked a utility armor, and supported requests for the Character Customizer.
- Art (Ships): The Ships team progressed with the RSI Zeus, continuing with the beauty and polish stage.
- Audio: For the upcoming Alpha 3.23 release, the Audio Vehicle team completed their first milestone in overhauling the ship audio experience with new thruster sounds, which is rolling out to all new ships.
- Community: The Community team started the month by celebrating Triggerfish with the announcement of the MISC R.A.P.T.O.R, the ultimate weapon in the war against garbage!
- Core Gameplay: In April, the Core Gameplay Pillar closed out features and prepared them for release in Alpha 3.23.
- In-Game Branding: Last month, the Branding and Vehicle teams worked closely to create brand identities for upcoming and existing vehicles within the game.
- Interactables: The Interactables team completed their work on fire extinguisher recharge cabinets, including both high-tech and low-tech versions.
- Lighting: Lighting spent time in April polishing Distribution Centers before moving on to instanced hangars and freight elevators, with the aim of making every interaction an engaging event.
- Locations: The Locations teams spent April closing out features for Alpha 3.23.
- Mission Design: Last month, Mission Design continued to polish content for Alpha 3.23, including XenoThreat and fauna-related missions.
- Narrative: April was a very busy month for the Narrative team, who worked hard preparing for the Alpha 3.23 patch.
- Online Technology: After several sprints, the Online Services Team completed their refactor of the social services backend.
- R&D: R&D spent April supporting Alpha 3.23.
- Tech Animation: The Tech Animation team continued to generate and implement new head assets to the DNA gene pool, and are not far from completing the initiative of 40 heads for each gender.
- Tech Design: Tech Design provided general tech support for Alpha 3.23, including fixing bugs affecting doors and fuel tanks not exploding in the new Distribution Centers.
- UI: In April, the Montreal-based team focused on the Cargo feature and worked closely with Core Gameplay on the Resource Network mandate, which included getting wireframes signed off.
- VFX: Last month, the VFX team focused on bug fixing for the upcoming patch.

- Release View: As part of our final review process, we've concluded that the quality of the Cargo features that were targeting the launch of Alpha 3.23.0 are not yet at the stage where we need them to be for a…
- Vulkan Graphics API Support: Converting the Star Citizen renderer from DirectX11 to the Vulkan Graphics API.
- Water Simulation & Rendering Improvements: The water in Star Citizen now support a multi-scale GPU wave simulation to support dynamic reaction to thrusters, aerodynamic wake, explosions and collisions.
- mobiGlas Rework: Reworking the mobiGlas system to use Building Blocks, which will also allow for easier development of mobiGlas apps.
- FPS Loot Screen: Introducing a new screen for looting critical items quickly, allowing for more reliable inventory management in tense situations.
- FPS Map System: Implementing a minimap for the HUD as well as interior maps for FPS gameplay, helping players stay oriented in close-quarter encounters.
- Visor & Lens HUD Rework: Converting the Visor and Lens systems to Building Blocks for improved performance and flexibility.
- Player Interaction Experience: Implementing the updated Player Interaction Experience; a holistic array of complimentary features and systems, all related directly to the player.
- EVA T2: Improved EVA controls and animations for smoother traversal in Zero-G.
- Starmap Rework: Implementing the new and improved Starmap with improved visuals and usability, including easier search and trip planning functionality.
- Master Modes: Implementing new modes to vehicles to manage their speed, components, and role-specific functions.
- New Missions - Creature Hunting: New missions that require players to locate, kill and retrieve valuable parts of creatures roaming the environment.
- Fauna - Kopion: Populating the persistent universe with the Kopion, an aggressive, agile animal that travels in packs.
- Fauna - Marok: Populating the persistent universe with the Marok, a passive flying bird-like creature.
- Arena Commander: Engineering Experimental Mode: Three Limited Test Experimental Modes featuring the engineering gameplay (also referred to as "Resource Network") showcased at CitizenCon 2953.
- Arena Commander: Grav Royale: Embark on high-speed mayhem in a thrilling new game mode: Grav Royale!
- Arena Commander: Custom Lobbies: Custom Lobbies, previously referred to as “Private Matches”, makes their return to Arena Commander.
- Arena Commander: New Flight Map - Miner's Lament: Miner's Lament, previously exclusive to racing & part of the Master Modes tests, now opens its treacherous asteroid-laden expanse to all flight modes.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: May 2024
summary: Welcome to May’s PU Monthly Report! With Alpha 3.23 live our team from around the hglobe spent the month polishing features, squashing bugs, and progressing with the wealth of new content coming in 3.23.2, 4.0, and beyond. Read on for all the details.
digest:
Welcome to May’s PU Monthly Report! With Alpha 3.23 live our team from around the globe spent the month polishing features, squashing bugs, and progressing with the wealth of new content coming in 3.23.2, 4.0, and beyond. Read on for all the details.
- AI (Features): Following the launch of Alpha 3.23, AI Features supported the upcoming point patch and future releases.
- AI (Tech): Last month, AI Tech supported Alpha 3.23 with bug fixing and optimizations.
- Animation: In May, Gameplay Animation focused work on numerous creatures, including the unreleased Quasi Grazer ("space cow").
- Art (Characters): In May, the Character Art team completed the high-poly phase for two specialist armors and continued updating the utility armor.
- Art (Ships): For Alpha 3.23, Ship Art delivered the Aegis Retaliator’s cargo and bomber modules, ensuring they met gold-standard requirements.
- Community: The Community team began May supporting Alpha 3.23: Adventure Beckons, including the Mirai Pulse grav-lev bike.
- Core Gameplay: The Core Gameplay Pillar spent May closing out tasks and bug-fixing for Alpha 3.23 and 3.23.1.
- Economy: Last month, the ‘effort vs reward’ algorithm was documented, which enabled the Economy team to determine the technicalities of implementing the mission-system refactor.
- Interactables: Last month, liquid-carrying cargo containers were worked on, with all sizes moving from whitebox to final.
- Lighting: Lighting spent time finalizing work on instanced hangars.
- Locations: May saw the Landing Zone team fixing bugs for instanced hangars before moving on to mandates for Alpha 4.0, including crafting the remaining stations for Pyro.
- Mission Design: Throughout May, Mission Design continued working on cargo missions, specifically polishing the 'abandon' flow.
- Narrative: May kicked off with a flurry of activity for the Narrative team.
- Online Technology: In May, the Online Services team focused on wrapping up the social-services backend refactor, which will improve the performance and scalability of social features, including Chat, Friends, and…
- R&D: The R&D team’s support for Alpha 3.23 continued throughout May.
- Tech Design: Tech Design supported multiple areas of development for upcoming release patches, including resolving bugs related to creatures, interactables, cargo hangars and item banks, weapons, and performance…
- UI: The Montreal-based UI team worked on a variety of mandates in May, including tasks for cargo, ensuring all visual elements were polished and any bugs were thoroughly fixed.
- VFX: Like other teams, the VFX team put the finishing touches on their work for the Alpha 3.23 patch, fixing last-minute bugs and polishing effects where safe to do so.
- Web Platform: The Web Platform teams concentrated on preparing for the anticipated traffic surges during Invictus Launch Week.

- Progress Tracker: As you might have seen in the recent Letter From the Chairman, our development team is in the process of outlining the necessary tasks to achieve Star Citizen's full 1.0 commercial release.
- Arena Commander: Grav Royale: The team encountered a critical issue with this game mode that requires additional testing.
- Distribution Centers: Creating new traversable areas offering gameplay opportunities in corporate industrial environments.
- Vulkan Graphics API Support: Converting the Star Citizen renderer from DirectX11 to the Vulkan Graphics API.
- Water Simulation & Rendering Improvements: The water in Star Citizen now support a multi-scale GPU wave simulation to support dynamic reaction to thrusters, aerodynamic wake, explosions and collisions.
- Volumetric Clouds Update: Updating Star Citizen's volumetric cloud technology to improve overall visual quality and performance, including the addition of both volumetric shadows as well as the implementation of ground fog.
- Image Upscaling: Implementing support for GPU upscaling, including DLSS, FSR, and an in-house TSR solution.
- Replication Layer Update: Over the course of the 3.23 patch cycle, the Replication Layer will be moved off of the game servers and set up as its own standalone service.

title: Roadmap Roundup - May 15, 2024
summary: Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen
digest:
Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible. With that said, let’s go ahead and dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!
- Release View: In this week's Roadmap update, we're excited to announce the addition of Alpha 4.0 to Release View, targeting Q3 of this year.
- Server Meshing V1: The initial implementation of Server Meshing enables multiple servers per shard to improve load distribution and facilitates navigation between two solar systems.
- Mission System Refactor: Reworking the underlying Mission System to become compatible with Server Meshing, allowing for easier creation and maintenance of mission content.
- Transit System Refactor: Reworking the Transit System used for trams and elevators to be compatible with Server Meshing as well as generally more robust.
- Pyro I: Pyro I is the first planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro II - Monox: Monox (Pyro II) is the second planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro III - Bloom: Bloom (Pyro III) is the third planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro IV: Pyro IV is the outermost moon of Pyro V, and astronomers theorize that it was once the fourth planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro V: Pyro V is the fourth planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro VI - Terminus: Terminus (Pyro VI) is the outermost world of the Pyro system.
- Ignis: Ignis is the innermost moon of the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Vatra: Vatra is the second moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Adir: Adir is the third moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Fairo: Fairo is the fourth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Fuego: Fuego is the fifth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Vuur: Vuur is the sixth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Pyro Space Stations: Adding rundown rest stop stations to the Pyro system, which provide basic services such as repair, sustenance, and commerce.
- Outposts - Colonialism: A small home for AI to live and shelter.
- Jump Points: Implementing the first jump point into the persistent universe, connecting the Stanton and Pyro systems together.
- Solar Burst: Solar Bursts are dangerous natural disasters that happen regularly around older stars like Pyro.
- Life Support: Implementing the first iteration of onboard life support systems in ships, which entails a ship component that generates breathable gas when turned on, and management of said life support component…
- Engineering: Allows players to manage, maintain and repair various ship systems.
- Charge/Drain: Adding the ability for players to drain, store, and charge objects with power using the multi-tool.
- Multi-Tool Updates: Raising the multi-tool up to the standard from Squadron 42, with additional functionality like cutting (for specific scenarios), repair, and updates like improved handling, integrated UI, and the use…
- Fire Hazard: Implementing the Fire Hazard system, which tracks fire & temperature on static and dynamic objects.
- Fire Extinguisher: All tasks required to implement functioning fire extinguishers in-game.
- MFD Rework and New Displays: Rebuilding ship multi-function displays in Building Blocks, including new design, functionality, and customization options.
- Quasi Grazer: These large, warm-blooded herd animals were originally discovered on the vast plains of Quasi on Terra.
- Additional Player Customization: Following the release of the new character customizer in Alpha 3.23, this update adds additional hair and facial hair options, as well as face piercings.
- RSI Zeus MkII ES: Building, balancing, and implementing RSI's small multi-crew ship, the Zeus MkII ES, into the game.

title: Squadron 42 Monthly Report: July 2024
summary: Welcome to July’s Squadron 42 development report. Enclosed you will find details on the latest progress made across the campaign, including AI group combat, EVA updates, and additional narrative detail.
digest:
This is a cross-post of the report that was recently sent out via the monthly Squadron 42 newsletter. We’re publishing this a second time as a Comm-Link to make it easier for the community to reference back to. TO: SQUADRON 42 RECRUITS SUBJ: DEVELOPMENT UPDATE 08:07:2024 REF: CIG UK, CIG DE, CIG LA, CIG TX, FAO Squadron 42 Recruits. Welcome to July’s Squadron 42 development report.
- AI (Features): Last month, the AI Features team worked on a combination of fixes and new functionality, including an issue requiring a usable to have an interactable component.
- AI Tech: For AI Tech, support was given to the Design teams, with the devs implementing and exposing small functionalities alongside performance improvements.
- AI (Social Strike Team): July saw the AI Social strike team introduce new welding helmet animations for engineers in ship corridors, enhancing visual detail, and updating post-welding animations.
- Features (Gameplay): Gameplay Features continued improving control surfaces, addressing various tuning issues.
- Gameplay Story: At the start of July, the Gameplay Story team maintained and improved several scenes in the campaign’s early chapters.
- Narrative: Following on from last month’s report, Narrative tested their work on the in-game Galactapedia and began addressing user-experience improvements, including considerations for UI elements to make…
- UI: Last month, the UI team continued polishing in-world screens, optimizing a few existing levels to improve frame rate and creating medical screens for various scenarios.
- VFX: Finally for July’s report, the VFX team continued to support the Cinematics, Design, and Art teams in various polishing tasks.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: July 2024
summary: Welcome to July’s PU Monthly Report. With the upcoming Alpha 3.24 patch now live for testing in the PTU, many teams spent the month polishing and bug fixing alongside exciting new tasks for Pyro and beyond. Read on for all the details.
digest:
Welcome to July’s PU Monthly Report. With the upcoming Alpha 3.24 patch now live for testing in the PTU, many teams spent the month polishing and bug fixing alongside exciting new tasks for Pyro and beyond. Read on for all the details.
- AI (Features): Last month, the AI Features team worked on a combination of fixes and new functionality, including an issue requiring a usable to have an interactable component.
- AI (Tech): For AI Tech, the team continued working on the AI vision and movement systems for Server Meshing.
- Art (Characters): July saw the Character Art team begin work on utility armor.
- Art (Ships): July saw Ship Art working toward new milestones for the vehicles currently in production, including the RSI Polaris, Zeus, and three unannounced ships.
- Community: July began with the Community team supporting Foundation Festival 2954, which encouraged experienced players to share their knowledge with newcomers.
- Core Gameplay: The Gameplay Features teams progressed with a wide variety of features throughout July, beginning with ‘charge and drain.
- Economy: July saw the Economy team progressing with their tasks for Pyro, including the outer rings.
- In-Game Branding: In-Game Branding continued wrapping up tasks for jump points and the Pyro system, polishing content and ensuring everything fits the environment.
- Mission Design: Mission Design continued working on unannounced content alongside a suite that uses individual features to create a complex form of repair missions.
- Narrative: The Narrative team spent July continuing to support development for Alpha 4.0.
- Online Technology: In July, the Online Services team collaborated intensively with the Gameplay and UI teams to introduce a significant quality-of-life enhancement to freight kiosks: a search bar.
- UI: Last month, the UI designers and artists worked on the in-game visuals and functionality for the resource network UI and completed the final polishing tasks for jump points.
- VFX: Finally for July’s report, the VFX team continued to support several effects-heavy features, including jump points and dynamic fire.

- Notable Changes for July 24, 2024: The following cards have been added to Release View, targeting a release with Alpha 4.0:
- RSI Zeus MkII CL: Building, balancing, and implementing RSI's small multi-crew cargo ship, the Zeus MkII CL, into the game.
- Acidic Caves: Implementing the acidic cave archetype, coming to both the Pyro and Stanton systems.
- Rock Caves: Implementing the rock cave archetype, coming to both the Pyro and Stanton systems.
- Asteroid Bases: Implementing new asteroid bases scattered across space in asteroid clusters, gas clouds, and other areas of Pyro.
- Space Stations - Contested Zones: Contested Zones are a location feature coming to Pyro's space stations, introducing FPS gameplay with various layouts tailored for this purpose.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: August 2024
summary: Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! With the recent release of Alpha 3.24: Cargo Empires, most development teams spent the month both finalizing patch tasks and progressing with exciting new features coming further down the road. Read on for all the details.
digest:
Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! With the recent release of Alpha 3.24: Cargo Empires, most development teams spent the month both finalizing patch tasks and progressing with exciting new features coming further down the road. Read on for all the details.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features polished various reactions, including the ‘first reactions’ when AIs respond to audio or visual events.
- AI (Tech): AI tech continued to improve how NPCs transition between servers, including serializing movement requests and navigation paths.
- AI (Content): In August, the Social AI designers joined the Narrative team to form a larger group focused on improving the Star Citizen experience.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In August, the Game Intelligence Development team concentrated on delivering a clean and stable Apollo StarScript UX update.
- Animation: August saw the Facial Animation team developing content to flesh out more of the game world’s characters.
- Art (Characters): Character Art continued working on utility and specialist armors, while Character Concept Art supported IAE and progressed with their ongoing exploration of fauna.
- Art (Ships): Last month, Ship Art moved several unannounced vehicles toward their greybox reviews, while others approached their LOD-zero and final-content reviews.
- Community: In support of Alpha 3.24, the Community team made improvements and updates to the New Player and Welcome Back Pilot guides.
- Core Gameplay: Throughout August, the various Gameplay Feature teams continued to improve the hangar and cargo flows for Alpha 3.24 based on feedback from the PTU.
- Economy: The Economy team spent the month getting closer to uniting all their work into a cohesive economy consisting of ships, items, missions, fuel, consumables, freelancing, careers, and more.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: Alongside the ongoing stability and performance improvements for Vulkan, the Graphics team improved debug tooling for the long-term health of the dev experience.
- Interactables: The Interactables team spent time in August on items for Pyro mission content.
- Lighting: The Lighting team continued to support multiple areas of development, including Pyro’s space stations, acidic caves, and closeout work for Alpha 3.24.
- Locations: Last month, the Landing Zone team progressed with tasks for Alpha 4.0, including adding new areas and additional polish to Pyro’s space stations.
- Mission Design: Mission Design spent time in August updating the Salvage Mission archetype, enabling it to spawn ground panels and provide FPS gameplay at scrapyards.
- Narrative: The Narrative Team spent time last month working with Design and Branding to further develop the new Contested Zones and enhance the gameplay that players will experience there.
- Online Technology: In August, the Online Services team progressed with features scheduled for Alpha 4.0.
- VFX: The VFX team continued their support for jump points and dynamic fire, both of which were shown in recent episodes of Inside Star Citizen.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: September 2024
summary: It’s October, and that means one thing… CitizenCon approaches! Despite the impending festivities, development continued in earnest throughout the month, with teams across the globe progressing with content for Alpha 3.24.2 and beyond. Read on for all the details.
digest:
It’s October, and that means one thing… CitizenCon approaches! Despite the impending festivities, development continued in earnest throughout the month, with teams across the globe progressing with content for Alpha 3.24.2 and beyond. Read on for all the details.
- AI (Content): September saw the AI and narrative designers continuing their work in the Pyro system by setting up the spawn data and markup for the various outposts and space stations.
- AI (Features): With the upcoming release of Alpha 4.0, the AI Features team focused on locking down existing Human-combat features, including first reactions, ammo management, and tactics to ensure they work…
- AI (Tech): The AI Tech team began September focusing on Server Meshing, including how AI systems and components synchronize during server transition.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): The Game Intelligence Development team spent the month working toward the release of StarScript 1.0, with the main goal of improving how the tool feels to use.
- Animation: The Animation team spent most of September on the Argo ATLS alongside additional work on the kopion and other creatures.
- Art (Characters): In September, the Character Art team progressed with the utility and specialist armors, new heads for the character customizer, and tasks for the IAE event.
- Art (Ships): The Vehicle Content team moved several vehicles into their final phases, including the RSI Polaris and several unannounced ships.
- Community: The Community team began September supporting Alpha 3.24.1 with the Argo ATLS Q&A and by gathering feedback on live releases to help fix bugs and player issues.
- Core Gameplay: Core Gameplay began September supporting the Argo ATLS, which included unique tractor beam behavior that the team are looking to improve and expand moving forward.
- Economy: The Economy team continued their ongoing work on Pyro and began implementing some of the balance changes mentioned in previous Monthly Reports.
- Locations: The Landing Zone team continued the push toward Alpha 4.0, polishing and optimizing content and supporting the Design team in making Pyro as distinct as possible.
- Mission Design: Mission Design continued working on location repair missions, moving some of them into a ‘handyman’ archetype.
- Narrative: The Narrative team continued their support for Alpha 4.0’s upcoming missions.
- Online Technology: The Online Services team began September working on features for Alpha 4.0, including the updated mission and marker systems.
- UI: The UI team focused on multiple screens for the Pyro system while continuing close collaboration with the Core Gameplay Pillar on jump points and the resource network.
- VFX: VFX continued their tasks for jump points and supported the Vehicle, Weapons, and Location teams with a variety of deliverables, including the Argo ATLS and RSI Zeus Mk II.

A special modifier inside the GEO can be activated to reduce the laser’s power to suit the demands of FPS mineables. Can I swap out the GEO's mining laser for other S0 mining lasers, a salvage beam, or a tractor beam?

'Golem' is fairly unique to the Drake naming convention. What inspired this? “We were just looking at the industrial workhouse aspect of the ship and thinking of names that had a utilitarian, workhorse vibe.

title: Alpha 4.1: Orbital Assault - A Fight For Life
summary: As imprints begin to fail, previously restricted scientific research is underway once more, and that means an increased demand for rare resources.
digest: Imprints are failing. Regen is collapsing. Death is coming to call. Under new instruction from Imperator Addison, previously restricted scientific research is underway once more, and that means an increased demand for rare resources. With lives and mega profits on the line, greed, panic and fierce competition are inevitable. Keep your head, get the job done, and don’t go it alone. The Empire needs you to stop this crisis. Bring In the Big Gun Grab a handful of your most trusted allies to navigate Daymar’s orbital platform and activate its formidable, planetary laser.

title: Argo ATLS GEO - Mining Mechs
summary: Built upon the tried and tested ATLS power suit, the new GEO’s mining augmentations provide everything you need to streamline your excavation efforts.
digest: BEYOND POWER AND PRECISION Built upon the tried and tested ATLS power suit, the GEO’s industrial augmentations provide everything you need to streamline your excavation efforts. From its enhanced maneuverability to the bespoke mining tool, Argo’s dynamic new addition helps you work smoother, not harder. IT’S ONE GIANT LEAP FOR ARGO Argo has upped your mining game with the GEO’s bespoke mining laser. Built to extract ore and store it in the convenient bespoke 10 centiSCU (cSCU) backpack, the GEO makes constant maneuvering back and forth a thing of the past.

title: Drake Golem - For the Workers
summary: Enterprise is for everyone. Start your mining career with the Drake Golem.
digest: NEW SHIP, SAME DRAKE VALUES For the workers who keep the wheels of industry turning, Drake is proud to deliver our first mining ship, the Golem. This accessible tool finally ends the corporate monopoly on mining and places your future firmly within your grasp. Built for professional mining and little else, the Golem is well set to become the go-to choice of the hardest laborers in the galaxy. The Golem’s small but effective mining beam turns breaking rocks and small asteroids into quick work. The retractable mining arm is deployed from above to give you the best view of the task in hand.

title: Squadron 42 March Newsletter Comm-Link
digest: Humanity’s hostile relationship with the Vanduul began almost 300 years ago after the alien species unexpectedly raided a civilian outpost in the Orion system. This first contact cost countless Human lives, as has every encounter since. The Vanduul home world is unknown, their command structure is obscure, and with so little intel available to anticipate their agenda, all diplomatic efforts to improve Human-Vanduul relations have failed. It seems that the only language they understand is violence, but as Humans, we must continue to rise above. Enlist and help today’s Vanduul become tomorrow's vanquished.

title: Loremakers: Community Questions
summary: The Narrative Team answers your questions about the Valakkar, meaning of ATLS, whether Terra is safe from the Vanduul, and much more.
digest:
Welcome to Loremakers: Community Questions, a series focused on answering your lore quandaries and conundrums. We’ve done a deep dive through the lore Ask A Dev section and selected ten questions to answer about the Star Citizen universe. Questions were edited for context and clarity but you can click on the topic to go directly to the original post and join the conversation.
- Was the UEE Advocacy Retconned?: Question: The CitizenCon presentation showed a list of guilds for 1.0 but there was no mention about the UEE Advocacy.
- How Does the Terra Faction Justify the System Being so Exposed to Vanduul Attack?: Question: The Vanduul can reach Terra with three jumps and pass through undefended systems.
- How Did the Valakkar Migrate to Monox?: Question: Valakkar have been stated as being native to Leir III.
- Lore Before the 2070s?: Question: The last Galacatapedia update mentioned that Humans visited Luna in SEY 1969, which aligns with real life (duh).
- Forgotten Kruger Intergalactic?: Question: I feel like Kruger is one of the forgotten brands.
- How Does IP Law Work In-Universe?: Question: With the coming ability to acquire blueprints and create our own ripoff or improved versions of popular manufacturers' weapons, ships and other goods, how does IP law work in the UEE?
- Argo ATLS Acronym Meaning?: Question: The names of Argo vessel models correspond to acronyms:
- What's the Difference between Nyx I and Monox?: Question: From the descriptions, Nyx I seems to be a very similar planet to Monox/Pyro II.
- Presence of Imperator Addison?: Question: Will we get an updated model of her?
- Where Did the Name for The Ponos Boots Come From?: Question: While playing with a friend, we quite by chance found boots named Ponos/Понос, which translates from Russian as diarrhea.

To commemorate its introduction to the persistent universe, we asked the vehicle team to provide an update to its original Q&A alongside a few questions from the community. What role does the Polaris fill in the current Persistent Universe? The Polaris is the first military capital ship to arrive in the Persistent Universe, setting the standard for capital ships in Star Citizen. “Fast and lethal.

title: IAE 2954 Roberts Space Industries
summary: The Polaris corvette has arrived.
digest: Of course, the main attraction for RSI heads at this year’s expo is the hotly anticipated Polaris, a capital-class corvette designed to take down even bigger, nastier ships. Don’t let those huge guns distract you from the rest of RSI’s classic lineup, though, as it offers something for every pilot.

title: RSI Polaris - Built for the Modern Fight
summary: With massive torpedoes designed to take out much larger ships, a small-craft hangar, and a military-standard med bay, the Polaris singlehandedly keeps your local star system safe and secure.
digest: Born back in 2946 in response to the rapidly escalating Vanduul conflict, the swift and deadly Polaris corvette has become a mainstay of Naval patrols across the galaxy. With massive torpedoes designed to take out much larger ships, an on-board hangar, and a military-standard med bay, the Polaris punches well above its weight class and is just as capable on long-range patrol missions as it is keeping your local star system safe. Download the full RSI Polaris tech specs Blue, grey, and yellow Gold and matte black. Available exclusively to members of the Chairman’s Club.

title: IAE 2954 Esperia
summary: Esperia’s fully-flyable replicas allow you to re-live history and discover lost art.
digest: Esperia allows you to literally fly history with its meticulously recreated ships and vehicles. Whether the designs pull from the lost archives of our alien brethren or our own proud history, Esperia’s shipcraft never fails to amaze.

title: IAE 2954 Banu
summary: Get a closer look at the Banu’s unique approach to crafting their popular fighters.
digest: The Banu have a tradition of honoring their most revered designs by ‘borrowing’ them and mashing them together into craft that are unmistakable in their intentions. See for yourself how this time-tested technique turns out some of the galaxy’s meanest fighters.

title: IAE 2954 Aopoa
summary: Get up close and personal with the cutting edge of Xi’an fighting tech.
digest: Aopoa’s fearsome fighters give Human pilots a taste of the incredible maneuverability and fluidity Xi’an craft possess. Truly remarkable in action, Aopoa ships boast unprecedented handling thanks to patented thruster tech and unique positioning.

title: IAE 2954 Gatac Manufacture
summary: See why Gatac’s Human hybrids have taken the market by storm.
digest: Gatac continues to make strides in the Human/Xi’an hybrid market as its fluid and functional haulers become staples of Stanton stations and the surrounding spacelanes. See for yourself what all the fuss is about.

title: IAE 2954 MISC
summary: The Starlancer Series expands MISC’s fleet and your hauling operation.
digest: MISC claims its vehicles are “built for life” - a look at its versatile lineup of well-proven workhorses makes it hard to argue. With an eclectic range of haulers, miners, and nuanced career vehicles, MISC ensures you’re ready to take on whatever life throws at you, from the mundane to the utterly unpredictable.

title: IAE 2954 Mirai
summary: Mirai continues to defy the limits of performance.
digest: Settling nicely into its niche, Mirai makes a rare breed of vehicle. Almost more animal than machine, these ships and bikes take speed, handling, and power into the proverbial stratosphere, unleashing ferocious performance in sport and combat.

title: IAE 2954 Aegis Dynamics
summary: No strangers to the Expo, Aegis continues to be a convention favorite year in and year out.
digest: What can be said of Aegis Dynamics that hasn’t already been written in the annals of warfare? The storied brand continues to serve the private sector as it has the military all these years.

title: Q&A: Crusader Intrepid
summary: Now that Crusader Industries has made its debut on the starter-ship scene, we posed a few questions to the Vehicle team about the new light freighter. Here are the answers, straight from the designers themselves.
digest: Now that Crusader Industries has made its debut on the starter-ship scene, we posed a few questions to the Vehicle team about the new light freighter. Here are the answers, straight from the designers themselves. What prompted the naming of the ship "Intrepid? Since this is a starter cargo ship, we imagined the enterprising spirit of someone starting up a new transport business in the 'verse and thought that ‘Intrepid’ captured their plucky, adventurous attitude. Also, in its favor was the fact that there have been numerous real-life vessels with the designation ‘Intrepid’, which gave the name authenticity.

title: Loremakers: Community Questions
summary: The Narrative Team answers your questions about how XenoThreat keeps sneaking into Stanton, how old you need to be to join the UEE Navy, and much more.
digest:
Welcome to Loremakers: Community Questions, a series focused on answering your lore quandaries and conundrums. We’ve done a deep dive through the lore Ask A Dev section and selected ten questions to answer about the Star Citizen universe. All questions were edited for context and clarity but you can click on the topic to go directly to the original post and join the conversation.
- Who Are the Private Security Officers Stationed Around Orison?: Question: I call them "Ajax Security" because that's what their uniform style is called, but who are they really?
- How Is XenoThreat Accessing the Pyro-Stanton Jump Point?: Question: Recently, it was mentioned that ATC will have the ability to deny ships access to a jump point by remotely jamming the ship's jump drive.
- Timeline Incongruity With Rest & Relax in Pyro?: Question: There appears to be a timeline issue with the new stations in Pyro.
- Do You Often Incorporate Game Errors Into Lore?: Question: How much of that do you actually do?
- UEE Special Forces Units?: Question: I have a question regarding the nature of special forces units in the UEE military.
- Location of Trise System?: Question: I was poring over the Starmap, for reasons, when it struck me that this was listed as Banu system, yet it seems like it should be Xi'an.
- Discrepancy in the Whitley's Guide on the Carrack?: Question: The Whitley's Guide on the Carrack says this:
- Castra System and Empire Recognition?: Question: I'm confused on Castra System’s status with the empire.
- UEE Navy Enrollment Age?: Question: I've searched through the Galactapedia extensively to find the minimum age required to serve in the UEE Military/Navy, but I haven't had any luck.
- Any Plans to Make the Galactapedia Accessible Within the Game?: Question: I think it would be cool to be able to access the Galactapedia from a screen, like a mobiGlass for example.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: October 2024
summary: October was a busy month for all CIG staff, with patch launches, Pyro in the PTU, and (of course) CitizenCon 2954. Alongside these major events, progress on upcoming features continued, with many teams finalizing content for Alpha 4.0 and 2025. Read on for all the details.
digest:
October was a busy month for all CIG staff, with patch launches, Pyro in the PTU, and (of course) CitizenCon 2954. Alongside these major events, progress on upcoming features continued, with many teams finalizing content for Alpha 4.0 and 2025. Read on for all the details. To note, this will be the last PU Report of the year, with November and December’s entry coming in January. We’ll see you next time!
- AI (Content): Last month, the AI Content team supported the social behaviors tied to Stanton’s derelict outposts and settlements, which will be used for new mission content.
- AI (Features): October saw AI Features improving Human combat features for Alpha 4.0.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech continued to support Server Meshing, synchronizing the Subsumption component between dedicated servers so that NPCs continue their assigned behaviors when switching.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): Throughout October, the Game Intelligence Development team polished StarScript v1.0 for its internal release.
- Animation: Last month, the Animation team worked on the valakkar and ‘space cow’ alongside adjustments to the kopion.
- Art (Characters): In October, the Character Art team focused on tasks related to CitizenCon.
- Art (Ships): October saw the Ship team complete the final content review for the RSI Polaris, while the final content tasks are currently in progress for the MISC Starlancer MAX.
- Community: The Community team began the month supporting Day of the Vara with the Pumpkin Decorating and Killer Klips from Outer Space contests.
- Economy: The Economy team continued their ongoing work on Pyro and began implementing some of the balance changes mentioned in previous Monthly Reports.
- Mission Design: In October, the Mission Design team finalized the Save Stanton quest chain.
- Narrative: The Narrative team tackled a multitude of tasks in the leadup to CitizenCon alongside ongoing work outside of the event.
- Online Technology: In October, the Online Services team progressed with features for Alpha 4.0.
- R&D: The R&D team spent the last few months supporting the introduction of dynamic weather.
- VFX: October saw the VFX team supporting various CitizenCon presentations, including those featuring new biomes, base building, and Levski.

summary: Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. digest:
Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible. With that said, let’s go ahead and dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!
- Star Citizen 1.0: Following the reveal of Star Citizen 1.0 at CitizenCon 2954, we’re excited to introduce a new addition to Release View in the Public Roadmap.
- Release View: The following cards have been added to the Alpha 3.24 column on Release View:
- MISC Starlancer MAX: Building, balancing, and implementing MISC's large multi-crew cargo ship, the MISC Starlancer MAX, into the game.
- Argo CSV-SM: Building, balancing, and implementing Argo's flatbed hauling ground vehicle, the Argo CSV-SM, into the game.
- RSI Polaris: Building, balancing, and implementing RSI's corvette, the Polaris, into the game.
- Anvil Hornet F7C-R Tracker MkII: Building, balancing, and implementing Anvil's pathfinding fighter, the Hornet F7C-R Tracker MkII, into the game.
- Anvil Hornet F7C-S Ghost MkII: Building, balancing, and implementing Anvil's stealth fighter, the Hornet F7C-S Ghost MkII, into the game.
- Acidic Caves: Implementing the acidic cave archetype, coming to both the Pyro and Stanton systems.
- Rock Caves: Implementing the rock cave archetype, coming to both the Pyro and Stanton systems.
- Additional Player Customization: Following the release of the new character customizer in Alpha 3.23, this update adds additional hair and facial hair options, as well as face piercings.
- Multi-Tool Updates: Bringing the multi-tool in line with Squadron 42, including adding additional functionality like cutting (for specific scenarios), repair, and updates like improved handling, integrated UI, and the…
- Life Support: Implementing the first iteration of onboard life support systems in ships, which entails a ship component that generates breathable gas when turned on, and management of said life support component…
- Engineering: Allows players to manage, maintain and repair various ship systems.
- Fire Hazard: Implementing the Fire Hazard system, which tracks fire & temperature on static and dynamic objects.
- Fire Extinguisher: All tasks required to implement functioning fire extinguishers in-game.
- Solar Burst: Solar Bursts are dangerous natural disasters that happen regularly around older stars like Pyro.
- Charge/Drain: Adding the ability for players to drain, store, and charge objects with power using the multi-tool.
- Transit System Refactor: Reworking the Transit System used for trams and elevators.

title: Roadmap Roundup - November 27, 2024
summary: Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen
digest:
Every two weeks, we accompany the Roadmap update with a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes. This is part of an effort to make our communications more transparent, more specific, and more insightful for all of you who help to make Star Citizen and Squadron 42 possible. With that said, let’s go ahead and dive into this week’s Roadmap Roundup!
- Release View: The following deliverables have completed final review for Alpha 4.0, therefore we are changing their status to Committed:
- Server Meshing V1: The initial implementation of Server Meshing enables multiple servers per shard to improve load distribution and facilitates navigation between two solar systems.
- Jump Points: Implementing the first jump point into the persistent universe, connecting the Stanton and Pyro systems together.
- Pyro I: Pyro I is the first planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro II - Monox: Monox (Pyro II) is the second planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro III - Bloom: Bloom (Pyro III) is the third planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro IV: Pyro IV is the outermost moon of Pyro V, and astronomers theorize that it was once the fourth planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro V: Pyro V is the fourth planet from the sun of the Pyro system.
- Pyro VI - Terminus: Terminus (Pyro VI) is the outermost world of the Pyro system.
- Ignis: Ignis is the innermost moon of the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Vatra: Vatra is the second moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Adir: Adir is the third moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Fairo: Fairo is the fourth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Fuego: Fuego is the fifth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Vuur: Vuur is the sixth moon from the gas giant Pyro V, Pyro system.
- Pyro Space Stations: Adding rundown rest stop stations to the Pyro system, which provide basic services such as repair, sustenance, and commerce.
- Fauna - Quasi Grazer: These large, warm-blooded herd animals were originally discovered on the vast plains of Quasi on Terra.
- Outposts - Colonialism: A small home for AI to live and shelter.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: November & December 2024
summary: It’s the first Monthly Report of 2025! To kick off the reporting year, we’re looking back to the end of 2024, detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe in November and December. Read on for all the details behind Alpha 4.0’s development and beyond.
digest:
It’s the first Monthly Report of 2025! To kick off the reporting year, we’re looking back to the end of 2024, detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe in November and December. Read on for all the details behind Alpha 4.0’s development and beyond.
- AI (Content): The AI team ended 2024 progressing with tasks for Alpha 4.0.
- AI (Features): In November and December, the AI Feature team progressed with combat for Pyro, particularly for Alpha 4.0’s Contested Zones.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech spent the last two months making performance improvements to AI systems and progressing with new features.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): Throughout November and December, the Game Intelligence Development team continued to close down StarScript 1.1, updating the old Apollo documentation to the new UX and adding documentation to the…
- Animation: November saw the Animation team create player-interaction animations for hacking and door panels.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team supported StarWear art debt and fixed bugs for the live releases.
- Art (Ships): The Ship Art team spent the end of 2024 putting the finishing touches on upcoming vehicles that will be revealed or released this year.
- Community: The Community team began the busy months of November and December with a recap of CitizenCon 2954 and by making all presentations from the event available on YouTube.
- Core Gameplay: All Core Gameplay teams were heavily involved in addressing stability and performance issues found during Alpha 4.0 PTU.
- Economy: The end of 2024 saw the Economy team adjust the prices of quantum and hydrogen fuel to account for new tank sizes.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: For the graphics department, the end of 2024 largely involved making significant performance and stability improvements to Alpha 4.0.
- Interactables: Interactables developed assets for Contested Zones, such as keycards, server blades, and fuse slots, and completed a performance and bug pass.
- Locations: The Locations team spent the end of 2024 supporting the Alpha 4.0 build, including polishing, optimizing, and bug-fixing Pyro’s Contested Zones and outposts.
- Mission Design: The ongoing mission refactor continued, with bugs being prioritized and triaged.
- Narrative: Over the past two months, the Narrative team focused on finishing mission content text for Alpha 4.0.
- Online Technology: In November and December, Online Services finalized the backend services crucial to several key features, including the mission-system refactor, the entity-subscription service/marker refactor, the…
- R&D: In November and December, the R&D team continued to finalize the core system components for the first version of dynamic weather.
- Tech Art/Animation: The Technical Animation team continued with a range of long-term tasks to facilitate improvements across the board.
- Tech Design: Throughout November and December, Tech Design primarily focused on the Contested Zones.
- VFX: In November, VFX supported the Vehicle teams with the Mirai Guardian and the Locations teams with a variety of Pyro location work.

summary: Welcome to January’s PU Monthly Report! Hot on the heels of the recent November/December report, we’re back detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe at the beginning of 2025.
digest:
Welcome to January’s PU Monthly Report! Hot on the heels of the recent November/December report, we’re back detailing everything done for the Persistent Universe at the beginning of 2025. Read on for all the latest updates on AI, core gameplay, missions, narrative, and much more.
- AI (Content): The AI Content team began the year prototyping an upcoming NPC that will utilize an amalgamation of several behavior types.
- AI (Features): In January, AI Feature’s primary focus was split between bug fixes and creature-behavior improvements.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): The Game Intelligence Development (GID) team continued their work on StarScript, with January’s goal being the implementation of the ‘views’ feature.
- AI (Tech): AI Tech began the year fixing bugs, improving features, and kicking off new tech.
- Animation: The Gameplay Animation team began the year working on the kopion hound and various sizes of the valakkar.
- Art (Characters): In January, the Character team continued working on StarWear art debt.
- Community: The Community team kicked off the year by announcing the winners of the Gift that Keeps on Giving video contest.
- Core Gameplay: Throughout January, the Core Gameplay teams investigated and improved many issues found during Alpha 4.0 Live Preview.
- Economy: The Economy team kicked off the year gathering feedback and data regarding the changes they implemented in Alpha 4.0.
- Mission Design: Mission Design spent time fixing bugs for Fight For Pyro, ensuring it was ready for release.
- Narrative: The Narrative team began 2025 meeting with multiple disciplines to solidify new ways of delivering in-game narrative content.
- Online Technology: In January, the Live Tools team released a new major feature to manage access and permissions in a more granular and versatile way.
- R&D: The R&D team began January investigating rare PU crashes inside the planet-spawning code.
- VFX: For Alpha 4.0.1, the VFX team worked on the MISC Fortune and elements of another vehicle, which will be shared soon.

summary: With the Roadmap just updated, here is a brief explanatory note to give you insight into the decision-making that led to any changes.
digest:
As we emphasized in the last Letter from the Chairman and throughout our messaging this year, our top priority for 2025 is improving playability. A key part of this effort is refining how we manage feature development—with features now being developed in a separate branch and only migrating over when they are ready.
- Release View: Deliverables released with 4.0.0 and 4.0.1 were marked as Released.
- Additions to the Star Citizen 1.0 column:: Improving atmospheric flight dynamics with functional control surfaces, allowing for more precise maneuvering and realistic aerodynamics.
- Progress Tracker: You can now find a preview of many of the things that we are currently actively working on in the Progress Tracker, with more additions to come at a later time.

summary: This month’s PU Report features progress on a variety of ongoing development initiatives, including the recently released Alpha 4.1, upcoming vehicles, AI work, and mission content. Read on for the latest updates!
digest:
This month’s PU Report features progress on a variety of ongoing development initiatives, including the recently released Alpha 4.1, upcoming vehicles, AI work, and mission content. Read on for the latest updates!
- AI (Content): For the recent debut of Star Citizen’s first alien NPC, Wikelo, AI Content worked alongside the Narrative Design, Design, Animation, Audio, and Character Art teams to prototype the character’s…
- AI (Features): In March, AI Feature’s priority was the valakkar, specifically the juvenile variant.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In March, Game Intelligence Development had two main focuses: the full implementation of Views and organization and analysis for Mission System 2.0.
- AI (Tech): Last month, AI Tech continued to work on features that will improve overall detail and quality, including finalizing work for the spatial priority solver and priority beacon system.
- Animation: The Animation team continued developing various sizes of valakkar alongside making updates to the kopion.
- Art (Characters): In March, the Character Art team continued to work on a new creature for the PU alongside StarWear art debt.
- Art (Ships): In March, the UK-based Vehicle Content team completed the Drake Golem mining ship and Argo ATLS GEO mining power suit.
- Community: The Community team kicked off March with support for Stella Fortuna, launching the Bar Crawl screenshot contest and publishing a catch-all post highlighting the exciting activities available to…
- Core Gameplay: For the Argo ATLS GEO, the Core Gameplay team completed the suit’s mining and thruster functionality, added a health bar and damage states, and supported additional improvements to the base ATLS.
- Economy: The Economy team provided balancing support for Supply or Die, with the devs deeming it over-tuned on release.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: Last month, the Graphics team overhauled GPU memory management.
- Mission Design: March saw Mission Design continuing to fix up various older missions that were deprioritized in the refactor.
- Narrative: Aligning with the increased release schedule cadence, Alpha 4.1 was a major focus for the Narrative team in March.
- Online Technology: In March, the Live Tools team focused on improving the usability of their main support tool, Hex.
- R&D: In March, gas cloud detail rendering was improved using techniques used by planetary volumetric clouds.
- Tech Design: Tech Design spent March working on an upcoming in-game event, supporting Mission Design with gameplay entity and logic flow setup.
- VFX: VFX progressed with their tasks for the valakkar.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: April 2025
summary: Welcome to April’s PU Monthly Report! With the UEEN Invictus fleet currently preparing to make the jump to Stanton, most teams touched on the upcoming festivities throughout the month. However, a lot of work was also done toward features and content coming later this year – read on for more de
digest:
Welcome to April’s PU Monthly Report! With the UEEN Invictus fleet currently preparing to make the jump to Stanton, most teams touched on the upcoming festivities throughout the month. However, a lot of work was also done toward features and content coming later this year - read on for more details.
- AI (Content): AI Content spent the majority of April preparing the release of Alpha 4.1.1, including the communications that players can now receive from mission givers.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features focused on refining the juvenile valakkar.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In April, the Game Intelligence Development (GID) team worked on various StarScript improvements, including allowing users to ‘right click’ task-extension links and search for an existing task to…
- AI (Tech): AI Tech progressed with the pathfinder system, making various improvements and cleaning up requests involving multiple start and end locations.
- Animation: Last month, the Animation team continued to support the studio-wide initiative of focusing on content for the PU.
- Art (Ships): In the EU, the team focused on closing out tasks for Invictus Launch Week, including three new ships planned for release at the event.
- Community: The Community team began April supporting Triggerfish, including the parody patch notes for the scaled-down EZ Hab Arena Commander Map.
- Core Gameplay: Several of the Core Gameplay teams spent the month stabilizing and improving the new space-themed missions in Alpha 4.1.1.
- Economy: Last month, the Economy team were involved in the new content coming in Alpha 4.1.1, including items and vehicles for Invictus.
- Mission Design: With most of their recent fundamental tech work complete, the team focused on improving mission quality.
- Narrative: In April, the Narrative team’s main focus was on a suite of new missions and support for Invictus Launch Week.
- Online Technology: In April, the Live Tools team worked on various features, including new sanction types and improvements to scheduling global system messages.
- R&D: In April, various improvements were made to the lightning evaluation that's part of the cloud and atmosphere raymarch.
- UI: Last month, the UI team worked to implement unique UI styles for several upcoming vehicles.
- VFX: Last month, VFX worked toward completing their tasks on vehicles and weapons for Invictus Launch Week.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: May 2025
summary: Alpha 4.2: Storm Breaker is live in the Public Test Universe! Although currently playable by anyone interested in contributing to development, there’s still a lot to do behind the scenes as the new content gets intentionally pushed to breaking point. Alongside patch fixes and tweaks, many teams touc
digest:
Alpha 4.2: Storm Breaker is live in the Public Test Universe! There’s still a lot to do behind the scenes as the new content gets pushed to the breaking point in preparation for Live release. Alongside patch fixes and other various changes, many teams touched on tech, locations, and updates coming later this year. Read on for all the latest info.
- AI Content: AI Content continued to support Star Citizen’s monthly release cadence.
- AI (Features): In May, AI Features ensured Human combat is in an optimal state in several key areas: ammo management and behavior, cover usage, first reactions and perception, attack and defend areas…
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In May, the Game Intelligence Development team began work on the UI prototype for Mission System v2; specifically the ‘outline header’ design, including the mission object properties design, the…
- AI (Tech): Last month, AI Tech continued to improve how navigation links connect to external zones.
- Animation: The Facial Animation team recorded and processed content for upcoming releases for both new and existing mission givers, including Wikelo.
- Art (Characters): May saw the Character Art team progress with new creatures, a heavy armor, and gameplay rewards.
- Art (Ships): As usual, May was extremely busy for the Vehicle Content teams as they supported new releases, progressed with upcoming vehicles, and kicked off projects for the next year or so.
- Community: The Community team spent much of May breaking down Community feedback/sentiment across all platforms and ensuring its delivery to the right teams internally.
- Core Gameplay: Core Gameplay are currently working through a long list of weapon improvements to further modernize the FPS experience for both Squadron 42 and Star Citizen, including tweaking how disruptive weapon…
- Lighting: Lighting supported all recent and upcoming patch releases, including adding environmental and dynamic lighting to interactable event locations in Pyro.
- Locations: The Locations teams continued to support the ongoing monthly content releases.
- Narrative: May brought with it a flurry of activity for the Narrative team.
- Online Technology: In May, the Network team continued work on Dynamic Server Meshing, separating the DGS assignment from the territory manager.
- UI: In May, the team completed the UI for an upcoming event, creating various screens to support the narrative and gameplay.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: June 2025
summary: June was a busy month at CIG, with most teams making final updates toward Alpha 4.2 and upcoming content. Read on for all the details of last month’s development, including the latest from the Ships, AI Tech, and Core Gameplay teams.
digest:
June was a busy month at CIG, with most teams making final updates toward Alpha 4.2 and upcoming content. Read on for all the details of last month’s development, including the latest from the Ships, AI Tech, and Core Gameplay teams.
- AI Content: June saw AI Content meeting with the directors and Combat AI team to keep pushing the development of the updated combatant wildline script.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features completed their tasks for the irradiated valakkar, which made its debut in the PU.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): The Game Intelligence Development team started the month with meetings relating to StarScript, Mission System 2.0, the commentator model, the density profiler, entity scripting, Mannequin, and the…
- AI (Tech): Throughout June, the AI tech team provided bug fixes and support for the Alpha 4.2 release, including optimizing how navigation-mesh regeneration accounts for navigation links.
- Animation: Animation spent the month supporting the irradiated valakkar alongside another new creature for later this year.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Anvil Paladin continued through greybox, with additional artists being moved onto it as their other tasks were completed to help prepare for its July gate review.
- Community: June began with a celebration of diversity and culture as the team launched Show Us Your Colors 2025.
- Core Gameplay: With the new Storm Breaker content, the Core Gameplay teams added several updates to radiation, hazard areas, and damage-over-time handling.
- Mission Design: Last month, Mission Design worked to close out the Storm Breaker sandbox activity for release.
- Narrative: Following Alpha 4.2’s release, the Narrative team focused on the next two upcoming patches, which will feature a variety of new missions.
- Online Technology: The Online Services team continued to work on the ‘item imprint system’- design aspects are being discussed, technical documentation is being written, and service development began.
- R&D: Gas cloud rendering was further refined based on the improvements implemented in March.
- VFX: The VFX Code and Art teams worked on several things for Alpha 4.2.

summary: With Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue’s Descent live and another action-packed update this month, the Star Citizen universe has never been more packed with adventure. Read on for everything done at CIG’s studios throughout September, from updated backend code to all-new missions and more.
digest:
With Alpha 4.3.1: Virtue's Descent live and another thrilling update this month, the Star Citizen universe has never been more packed with adventure. Read on for everything done at CIG’s studios throughout September in pursuit of this new content, from updated backend code to all-new missions and more.
- AI Content: The AI Content team continued to test updates to some of the landing-zone NPCs, looping in the QA team to help stress test the setup to ensure it can take the strain of extensive use and trigger any…
- AI (Features): AI Features updated numerous features last month, beginning with AIWeaponComponent, which will now remain in sync with weapon statuses, allowing them to work better in unison.
- AI (Tech): September saw AI Tech improve NPCs using elevators by simplifying the set up of the transit carriage.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In September, the Game Intelligence Development team focused on completing the next milestone for Mission System 2.0.
- Animation: The Animation team continued to work on an upcoming creature and ‘boss’ fight alongside supporting a new mission giver.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team finalized both new armors and a new gang.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, work continued to bring the RSI Aurora and Aegis Hammerhead up to modern standard.
- Community: The team kicked off the month with the grand finale of this year’s Ship Showdown, where the RSI Polaris claimed the crown.
- Core Gameplay: As part of ongoing medical gameplay improvements, the team provided support for bespoke ‘take’ and ‘place’ animations, and reworked the implementation of players clearing their respawn point in…
- Economy: The Economy team began the month exploring how to make the players’ impact on freelancing commodity trading more impactful and longer lasting.
- Mission Design: Mission Design began September finalizing the last narrative mission for the ASD facilities before looking forward to the rest of the year’s content.
- Narrative: In September, the Narrative team focused on tasks to help close out the rest of the year strongly.
- Online Technology: Last month, the Live Tools team updated the error reporting pipeline, including moving panic migration from Heap to Laravel.
- R&D: In September, the R&D team’s focus remained exclusively on analyzing performance and optimizing engine and game code.
- VFX: For Alpha 4.3.2, VFX finished up their tasks for the ASD locations and final event work, while the RSI Apollo Triage and Medivac received their VFX passes.

title: Traveler's Guide to the Galaxy: Nyx
summary: Welcome to another edition of Traveler’s Guide to the Galaxy. These dispatches aim to provide early insights into the lore and design shaping new locations coming to the Star Citizen universe. This time, we venture to Nyx, the third star system to join the ‘verse, coming in Alpha 4.4.
digest:
- Star System: Welcome to another edition of Traveler's Guide to the Galaxy.
- WELCOME TO THE NYX SYSTEM: Nyx is an unclaimed planetary system situated at the border of a dark nebula.
- Settlement: The system's primary settlement, Levski, is built into a large asteroid within the Glaciem Ring.
- THE TANAKA MEMORIAL: The entrance of Levski is dominated by a statue of an unnamed worker holding the lifeless body of Anthony Tanaka, a child laborer who was executed by an Advocacy agent in 2757 for refusing to…
- STRONGER TOGETHER: A faction originally formed by people fleeing the unjust Messer regime, they founded a utopian colony in a ready-made station on an asteroid in the Nyx system.
- NOTABLY NYX'S: Remote, rugged, and rich in character, Delamar has quietly become a source of some of the most distinctive drinks in the UEE.
- TRISE SLING: While Trise Cordial isn't native to Nyx, its most famous cocktail may well be.
- JYNX GIN: Distilled and bottled on Delamar, Jynx Gin owes its striking coloration and part of its mystique to the omphalotus mushroom.
- Beyond Alpha 4.4: What follows is a preview of content that's planned for future updates and not included in Alpha 4.4.
- LOCATIONS: New locations will arrive with future content drops.
- NYX I: A green yet uninhabitable world undergoing an experimental terraformation process, Nyx I may soon have an atmosphere that will let everyone breathe free.
- NYX II: The air on Nyx II is sweltering, stifling, and extremely poisonous.
- NYX III: Furthest planet from the star at the center of the Nyx system, Nyx III is an ice giant with a stormy atmosphere.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: October 2025
summary: Welcome to the latest PU Monthly Report! Read on for all the behind-the-scenes details of development throughout October, including progress on Nyx, upcoming ships, AI behaviors, the in-game economy, and more.
digest:
Welcome to the latest PU Monthly Report! Read on for all the behind-the-scenes details of development throughout October, including progress on Nyx, upcoming ships, AI behaviors, the in-game economy, and more.
- AI Content: In October, the Narrative and Social AI teams supported several initiatives for the upcoming Alpha 4.4 patch, including landing zone fixes.
- AI (Features): Last month, AI Features continued to iterate on first reaction and usable animations.
- AI (Tech): The AI Team made improvements to navigation-mesh generation, including to the generation algorithm.
- AI (Game Intelligence Development Team): In October 2025, the Game Intelligence Development team worked toward the next milestone for Mission System v2, focusing on implementing ‘outline properties’, the first pass of a prototype property…
- Animation: Animation worked on the Yormandi throughout October alongside improvements to the kopion.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team finalized various armors for a new gang and in-game rewards, and progressed with a new heavy armor and clothing items.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team supported the release of the Anvil Paladin, Esperia Stinger, and Grey’s Market Shiv at CitizenCon Direct.
- Community: October began with the return of Day of the Vara, the ‘verse’s spirited fall event, which the Community team supported with an informative thread and a pair of creepy contests.
- Core Gameplay: The Core Gameplay teams pushed forward on the inventory revamp.
- Economy: The team spent last month building the economy of Nyx and giving the system character.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: Folllowing the Preview Channel testing of Vulkan, the graphics team fixed many performance issues, the vast majority of which were caused by running out of video memory.
- Mission Design: Mission Design worked on the recent limited-time event, the Frontier Fighters Finale.
- Narrative: Last month, the Narrative team focused on the final preparations for the release of Nyx.
- Online Technology: October saw the Online Services team progress with Item Recovery T1 and the early stages of instancing.
- R&D: In October, the R&D team worked on engine optimizations that will eventually make their way into the PU.
- VFX: VFX supported all of the game’s upcoming vehicles, with some standouts being the Shiv and Stinger.

title: Galactic Guide: Nyx System
summary: Learn about one of Star Citizen’s “first five” systems!
digest:
Nyx was discovered in SEY 2582 during the height of the newly-formed United Empire of Earth’s territorial expansion. The system consists of three planets circling an F-type main sequence star and two asteroid belts. Astronomically, the most distinct aspect of Nyx is that it is located directly on the border of a dark nebula, which gave the system its name.
- Nyx I: When it was first discovered, Nyx I was a coreless, heat-swept world that was a poor colonization candidate.
- Nyx II: Cloaked in thick clouds of acid, Nyx II was once considered for terraforming due to its position within the system’s green band.
- Glaciem Ring Asteroid Belt & Delamar: A dense asteroid belt circles Nyx’s star between Nyx II and Nyx III.
- Nyx III: The final planet in the Nyx System, located far from the sun’s light, is an ice giant.
- Keeger Belt: This outermost asteroid belt has long been a favorite hiding place for those who would prefer to do their business in the shadows.
- Travel Warning: While Levski’s airlocks are open to visitors, they do ask that guests abide by the code of rules and morals that they’ve established or risk the resident’s ire.

title: Engineering Gameplay Guide
summary: A starter guide to developing Engineering gameplay.
digest:
- Engineering Gameplay Guide: A key pillar of Star Citizen’s vehicle gameplay loop is Engineering.
- WHAT IS ENGINEERING GAMEPLAY?: Engineering gameplay revolves around managing resources across your ships and vehicles through the Resource Network.
- TOOLS: All engineers need to consider the following necessary tools to perform their tasks:
- ENGINEERING ITEMS: These are the elements found within vehicles that will support the Engineering gameplay loop:
- Components: Core elements that drive the main functionality of major vehicle systems.
- Relays: Link systems together and allow resources to travel through the ship.
- MFD Power and Diagnostic: Provide a high level overview of power distribution and resource management.
- Engineering Console: The beating heart of Engineering in most ships with interiors, giving crew the tools to review power flow, allocate resources, control systems, and understand the ship’s overall state.
- WHAT ARE COMPONENTS?: Components provide the main functionality for all major vehicle systems; they are the core organs that keep the ship flying.
- ENGINEERING RESOURCES: Engineering gameplay is the physical expression of the Resource Network and the management that surrounds it.
- POWER DISTRIBUTION: Distributing power throughout your vehicle is one of the most important responsibilities for any engineer.
- ENGINEERING CONSOLE: The Engineering console is the central hub for monitoring and controlling system performance across the ship.
- COMPONENTS DETAILS: All components are linked through relays, allowing resources to move throughout your ship.
- LIFE SUPPORT THROUGH THE SHIP: Engineers must ensure that Life Support is always active throughout the ship to maintain a breathable atmosphere.
- ARMOR: In Alpha 4.5, ships gain Armor as an extra layer of defense.
- DAMAGE PENETRATION: Different weapon types perform better or worse against armor, creating opportunities to target internal systems more effectively.
- WEAR AND TEAR (Full System Coming Soon): Over time, if components are not properly maintained, they will suffer wear and tear that reduces their effectiveness.
- HEAT AND FIRE: Heat is now a crucial element for pilots and engineers to monitor.
- MALFUNCTIONS: Components that are damaged, worn, or running too hot can begin to malfunction, and the results can range from reduced performance, to complete shutdowns.
- CRITICAL FAILURE: Critical failures are catastrophic states that may cause your entire vehicle to explode.
- REPAIRING: Repair gameplay is essential to extending the life of all components and your vehicle as a whole.
- ENGINEERING AVAILABILITY IN ALL VEHICLES: As of Alpha 4.8, every single vehicle in Star Citizen is Engineering-enabled and capable of the baseline experience.

summary: Welcome to February’s PU Monthly Report! Read on for everything done toward this exciting upcoming release.
digest:
Welcome to February’s PU Monthly Report! There’s a huge amount of content coming to ‘verse in the next few weeks, including new and returning missions, the latest ships from RSI, and thrilling activities and locations around Nyx. Read on for everything done toward this exciting upcoming release.
- AI Content: The Social AI team began the month bug fixing in support of Alpha 4.6 before looking to future releases.
- AI (Features & Tech): Last month, AI Features & Tech improved underground traversal for the valakkar, prototyping its future speeds.
- Animation: Animation spent February improving assets for the kopion, while Facial Animation focused on the first performance-capture shoot of the year.
- Art (Characters): February saw Character Art polishing assets for Alpha 4.7 alongside working through art debt in preparation for StarWear.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team completed the art phases for the Aegis Hammerhead gold standard, with the ship moving to downstream teams for close-out.
- Community: The Community team began the month by publishing the January PU Monthly Report and preparing for February’s seasonal and community-driven events.
- Core Gameplay: As seen by Evocati players during recent Tech Previews, the Core Gameplay team made solid progress on the Inventory Rework.
- Economy: The Economy team spent part of February tracking exploits, in particular those that resulted in item duplication or large quantities of aUEC being generated.
- Mission Design: In February, the devs continued to work on the Alpha 4.7 mission pack, which adds more content to Nyx and revives the courier missions that have been waiting for a refactor since Alpha 4.0.
- Narrative: In February, the Narrative team focused their efforts on Alpha 4.7, which will expand the content available in Nyx.
- Online Technology: In February, the Network team focused on improving stability and reliability across Hybrid/DGS, resolving several high‑impact crashes, watchdog timeouts, and replication errors.
- R&D: In February, work on the improved ground fog continued; a dissipation model was implemented to simulate fog behavior during a full day/night cycle.
- VFX: In February, the VFX team focused heavily on supporting Alpha 4.7, contributing to the development of new locations, creatures, props, and vehicles as additional deliverables for Nyx came online.
