title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: March 2026
summary: Welcome to March’s Monthly Report. As usual, there was a huge amount of work going on across CIG’s global studios, from the final touches of Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock to exciting content coming soon and later in the year. Read on for all the details!
digest:
Welcome to March’s Monthly Report. As usual, there was a huge amount of work going on across CIG’s global studios, from the final touches of Alpha 4.7: Welcome to the Rock to exciting content coming soon and later in the year. Read on for all the details!
- AI Content: Last month saw AI make numerous fixes while continuing to build for the future.
- AI (Features & Tech): For Alpha 4.7, AI Features & Tech solved issues caused by inclusions after breaching and looked into various bugs.
- Animation: March saw the Animation team working on snake and worm-type enemies, including creating new behavior animations.
- Art (Characters): The Character Art team progressed with projects for Alpha 4.8 alongside in-game assets.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, the Ships team progressed with the Gatac Railen, preparing it for its greybox gate review at the end of March.
- Audio: Last month, the Audio team successfully delivered their work for Alpha 4.7.
- Community: The Community team kicked off March by publishing the February PU Monthly Report and laying the groundwork for an eventful month ahead.
- Core Gameplay: The Core Gameplay team spent part of March progressing hacking, with the devs polishing items, improving the tutorial, and ensuring the UI is always correctly aligned to the player.
- Creature Content: March saw the formation of a new team, Creature Content, to focus on the ongoing development of ‘Star Paws’ features.
- Economy: March saw the Economy team moving onto features for Alpha 4.8, which will bring new item crafting, commodity trading, and item recovery systems to the ‘verse.
- Game Intelligence Development: In March 2026, the Game Intelligence Development team primarily focused on the ongoing design and planning work for Mission System v2.
- Level Design (UK & DE): While March saw the Level Design teams progressing on a variety of locations, the primary focus was on Nyx’s social stations and QV Breaker Station locations, which went live in Alpha 4.7.
- Mission Design: Mission Design completed the second Nyx mission pack, which expands the amount of content for players, including moving some factions to utilize a reputation scope.
- Narrative: In March, the Narrative team continued tasks for a whole host of upcoming gameplay operations and missions.
- Online Technology: In March 2026, the Network team focused heavily on advancing the foundation for Server Meshing.
- R&D: In March, the ongoing ground-fog work continued.
- Tech Art/Animation: Over the past month, the Technical Animation team progressed with characters, creatures, interactables, cloth simulation, and the pipeline tools that support all of the above.
- VFX: For Alpha 4.7, VFX focused on finishing Nyx’s QV Breaker Station locations, such as the laser room and spacescaping, and hero moments, like the laser and asteroid interior.

Read on for everything that happened behind the scenes of the PU throughout April.
- AI Content: April saw the Narrative Design team introduce Tactical Strike Groups.
- AI (Features & Tech): AI Tech & Features began April with various optimization tasks, including a refactor of the Hermite cubic spline implementation to achieve better performance.

- Community: The Community team kicked April off with the publication of the March PU Monthly Report and early prep work for the Captains of Industry event.
- Core Gameplay: In April, Core Gameplay supported various initiatives and focused on bug fixing for Alpha 4.8.
- Mission Design: April saw the Mission team design fundamental changes to the contract system.
- Narrative: Narrative began April by wrapping up content for Alpha 4.8.
- Online Technology: In Montreal, the Live Tools team completed various improvements to the internal tools that keep Star Citizen's operations and development running smoothly.
- R&D: In April, further changes were made to the shader compile server to significantly improve robustness, latency, and throughput.
- Tech Art/Animation: Throughout April, the Technical Animation team continued to advance content across characters, creatures, armor, and the underlying pipeline.
- VFX: VFX worked through major tasks for Alpha 4.8, such as vehicles, including the Drake Ironclad, Tactical Strike Groups, and the Kastak Arms plasma grenade and UltiFlex Novia crossbow.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: May 2026
summary: Welcome to the PU Monthly Report! May saw Alpha 4.8 and DefenseCon hitting the ’verse, with many teams spending the month finalizing features for these major releases. Following this, tasks began and continued for the exciting content coming over the next few patches. Read on for all the details.
digest:
Welcome to the PU Monthly Report! May saw Alpha 4.8 and DefenseCon hitting the ’verse, with many teams spending the month finalizing features for these major releases. Following this, tasks began and continued for the exciting content coming over the next few patches. Read on for all the details.
- AI Content: Following the launch of Alpha 4.8, the AI Content team began closing out tasks for Alpha 4.9 and beyond.
- AI (Features & Tech): On the animation side, significant work went toward the mass retargeting of male-to-female combat AI assets, with additional support for unconscious and bleeding-out behaviors.
- Animation: Last month, the Animation team progressed with the apex valakkar, fleshing out various additional attacks and animations.
- Art (Ships): May’s DefenseCon saw many of the Ships team’s recent projects flyable in the PU, including the Aegis Tiburon and Hammerhead ’gold standard,’ the Origin M80, the MISC Starlite, and the Drake Pitbull…
- Art (Weapons): In May, the Weapons team ensured their content was ready for Alpha 4.8, including the Kastak Arms plasma grenade and UltiFlex Novian crossbow, and a handful of skins for upcoming events.
- Community: The Community team began May by preparing for the launches of Alpha 4.8: Tactical Strike and DefenseCon 2956.
- Economy: Alpha 4.8 saw the introduction of two major economy features: ship insurance adjustments and player-crafted items.
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: The majority of the Graphics team focused on optimization throughout May, making significant improvements that will come at a later date.
- Mission Design: Last month, the Mission Design team progressed with Recco Battaglia.
- Narrative: As mentioned in last month’s report, the Narrative team held a performance-capture session, which not only brought back a familiar face but also recorded lines for a revamped existing mission.
- Online Technology: In May, the Online Services team continued their work on several key player-facing features, including the Social Chat (MVP) feature, which is being built to enable in-game text communication between…
- R&D: May saw the R&D team implement tweakable (approximate) multi-scattering in gas clouds, similar to the multi-scatter solution used for planet clouds.

- Economy: Last month, the Economy team evaluated the economic data from the Alpha 4.8 release and worked to improve some of the underlying systems, such as repair and reclaim.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: July 2026
summary: Welcome to July’s PU Report! Last month saw continued progress across a wide range of development areas, from new vehicles and characters to backend tech and planet generation. Read on for all the details.
digest:
Welcome to July’s PU Report! Last month saw continued progress across a wide range of development areas, from new vehicles and characters to backend tech and planet generation. Read on for all the details.
- AI Content: Last month, AI Tech supported content for Alpha 4.9 and 4.10, including the reintroduction of Recco Battaglia.
- AI (Features & Tech): Last month, AI Features & Tech enhanced the ‘FlyTo’ behavior.
- Animation: Animation continued to work on the apex valakkar and its gameplay attacks alongside creating enter and exit animations for new vehicles.
- Art (Characters): In July, the Character Art team polished the upcoming super-heavy armor and supported the creation of ‘loadouts.

- Community: The Community Team began July by publishing the June PU Monthly Report and announcing the winners of the Show Us Your Colors Celebration and Xeno Craft Challenge contests.
- Economy: Chawla's Beach and Ashland commodity runs have landed well with the community, and the Economy team is looking forward to introducing more opportunities in the future that result in similar emergent…
- Graphics, VFX Programming & Planet Tech: July saw the Graphics team comparing GI and reflections to an offline path-traced reference and making various improvements.
- Narrative: Throughout July, the Narrative team worked on several major projects that serve to highlight the different ways that gameplay and story align.
- Online Technology: July saw the Network team focusing on two major areas.
- R&D: The R&D team’s July work covered two areas: adding snow and expanded weather behavior to the planet simulation, and improving cloud rendering performance.
- Tech Art/Animation: Last month, the Technical Animation team continued refining the DNA head pipeline that drives every character face in the ’verse, resolving alignment and expression issues across several…

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: August 2026
summary: Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! While most teams contributed toward Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison throughout the month, many devs continued with tasks for exciting content coming soon and further down the road. Read on for all the latest details.
digest:
Welcome to August’s PU Monthly Report! While most teams contributed toward Alpha 4.10: Siege of Orison throughout the month, many devs continued with tasks for exciting content coming soon and further down the road. Read on for all the latest details.
- AI Content: The recent Alpha 4.10 patch marked an exciting milestone for AI Content, with the re-release of Recco Battaglia and the introduction of a narrative-driven mission chain.
- AI (Features & Tech): AI Features and Tech spent August improving Starchitect, fixing nav-meshes, and progressing with Star Paws.
- Animation: Last month, animations were worked on for the apex valakkar, including for major attacks on ship targets.
- Art (Characters): In August, the Character Art team finalized a new combat armor set and its variants, completed Subscriber flair items, and progressed with a new type of armor.
- Art (Ships): The UK team began the month with a final polish pass on the Kruger Stingray after utilizing the PTU to catch a number of small bugs before its full release.
- Community: August began with the team supporting two ongoing events that started in July: Foundation Festival, which welcomes new pilots and celebrates the community members who help them find their way, and…
- Narrative: Work continued in August on generating mission text for the huge number of missions that will be arriving with Nyx I.
- Online Technology: Last month, the Online Services team focused on improving the reliability of missions and contracts, specifically the system that generates jobs and delivery tasks.
- R&D: August saw the R&D team working on planet atmosphere, including making improvements to the overcast skylight.
- Tech Art/Animation: Throughout August, the Technical Animation team focused on the systems that make characters look and move convincingly, including faces, deformation, cloth, and creatures.

title: Letter From The Chairman
digest: Thank you for supporting. Thank you for playing. Thank you for your feedback. It has been great to see more of you playing Star Citizen than ever before, with 35,890 concurrent players at our peak this year (and that wasn't even during a Free Fly!). And that growth goes well beyond a single peak. In the first half of 2026, we saw a 7% increase in average daily players and an 11% increase in monthly active players compared to last year. Seeing more of you playing and spending more time in the ‘verse has been incredibly rewarding for all of us at CIG.

Here are the answers, straight from the devs themselves. What is a "Quantum Dampener" and how is it different than a "Quantum Snare? These are two related technologies. A Quantum Dampener (QDMP) prevents ships within range from entering quantum travel. This is useful for keeping your target from escaping the fight. A Quantum Snare can force ships out of quantum travel.

title: Star Citizen Monthly Report: September 2026
summary: Welcome to September’s PU Monthly Report, featuring the latest updates from all the various disciplines working on Star Citizen. Read on for all the news from AI Features and Tech, Ships, Community, Core Gameplay, and more.
digest:
Welcome to September’s PU Monthly Report, featuring the latest updates from all the various disciplines working on Star Citizen. Read on for all the news from AI Features and Tech, Ships, Community, Core Gameplay, and more.
- AI Content: September saw AI Content looking into a new character type for mission gameplay, which will provide additional interactions and personality.
- AI (Features & Tech): AI Features and Tech worked on the apex valakkar, committing targeting fixes and bullet-bending refinements.
- Animation: Last month, animations were worked on for the apex valakkar, including for major attacks on ship targets.
- Art (Characters): Last month, Character Art had the final review of a new heavy armor releasing in Alpha 4.10.2.
- Art (Ships): In the UK, two unannounced vehicles both had final reviews ahead of their planned release alongside Genesis.
- Art (Weapons): The Weapon Content team completed a new Lightning Bolt Co. rifle alongside paints for upcoming events.
- Community: The Community team kicked off an activity-filled September by announcing Ship Showdown 2956's champion, the RSI Perseus.
- Core Gameplay: The last couple of months saw the Core Gameplay teams working through a long list of bugs and quality-of-life items, many of which were highlighted in the Improving the Live Experience Comm-Link.
- Mission Design: Last month, the Mission team rebalanced Bounty missions to bring them more in line with the recent ship updates.
- Narrative: In a very productive month, the Narrative team worked on several upcoming mission packs.
- Online Technology: Live Tools completed part two of the Hex 4.0 feature-parity work.
- R&D: The R&D team progressed with volumetric clouds, fixing an issue with occasional stale cloud shadow maps after fast camera movement.
